title: New missionaries to the Lamanites must keep to written revelation
setting: In September 1830, Oliver Cowdery and Peter Whitmer Jr. were called to preach to the Lamanites, meaning American Indians in the West. Other elders wanted these peoples to hear the Book of Mormon too, so Joseph Smith asked whether more should go. This revelation answered at Manchester, New York, in October 1830, probably before 17 October. It named Parley P. Pratt, baptized only weeks earlier, and Ziba Peterson, an elder licensed in June 1830. The missionaries left in late October and reached the Missouri border early in 1831.
summary: The revelation says Parley P. Pratt is to declare the gospel, learn of the Lord, and be meek and lowly of heart. He is to go with Oliver Cowdery and Peter Whitmer Jr. into the wilderness among the Lamanites. Ziba Peterson is to go with them as well. The Lord says he will go with them and be their advocate with the Father. Nothing shall prevail against them. They are to heed what is written and claim no other revelation. They are to pray always that the written word will be opened to their understanding.

contextNote.title: Bound to what is written
contextNote.text: The mission would take these men far from Joseph Smith, just after Hiram Page’s stone writings were rejected. Verse 4 sets their limits. They are to heed “that which is written” and “pretend to no other revelation”. The same verse tells them to pray for understanding of those writings. Verse 5 adds a warning to “trifle not”. Verse 3 explains why they could go without more instruction: the Lord promises to be in their midst. In this passage “pretend” means to claim, so the missionaries may not claim new revelation of their own.

ldsText: The Come, Follow Me 2025 lesson “Lift Up Your Voices … to Declare My Gospel” includes this call to the mission among the Lamanites. Verse 1 asks Parley Pratt to “learn of me” as well as preach; how do verses 1 and 4 link learning and teaching?
reviewNote: Read all 5 verses. Official heading gives Manchester, early October 1830, in answer to the elders’ wish to send missionaries to Indian tribes in the West.
